newsitem.title: UK: UK managers bullish on corporate prospects.
newsitem.headline: UK managers bullish on corporate prospects.

text.p: British managers are upbeat on their companies' business prospects over the next 12 months, an Institute of Management survey shows, posing an inflationary threat that demands interest rates rise soon.
The survey found 63 percent of the 280 managers canvassed were bullish about how their companies will perform over the next year, up from 59 percent in the previous quarter.

Furthermore, 56 percent of the managers reported an increase in consumer demand, an increase of 11 percentage points over the prior three months. About the same amount -- 57 percent -- expected consumer demand to keep rising over the next quarter.
"UK business is undoubtedly booming, but concerns are growing that confidence is turning into over-confidence," said Roger Young, the Institute's director-general.

He said there were signs that inflation was about to return. Only about a quarter of managers surveyed said they had increased prices but that reflected a rise of seven percentage points from the previous quarter. Nearly 30 percent said they are planning to raise prices.
"Prudence dictates interest rates should be top of any new government's agenda. It is time to draw in the horns of the bulls," Young said.
Elections are due on May 1 and the opposition Labour Party, riding high in the opinion polls, is hot favourite to win.

Sadly for Britain's managers, most did not expect to benefit personally from their firms' rosy prospects. 59 percent said they did not expect to be better off financially in 12 months time and nearly a third said they are insecure in their jobs.
